doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Finding Bird at the Apollo Bar with Gerry Mulligan
summary: Bird welcomes him from the stage and had told everyone about him; Bird's concern for others.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I said good Lord. So I put my wife in a hotel and that night I went over to this club and I walked in there and Gerry Mulligan was on the bandstand with his red hair and his red beard, he had this Ming the Merciless — remember this character Ming the Merciless in Flash Gordon?

With this long goatee. That’s the way Gerry had this long, red beard and a shock of red hair. And jeans, no socks and tennis shoes. That was how he was dressed on the bandstand. Well those guys were spending all their money on heroin. They were shooting up all day every day. And he was living uptown with Bird at that time. And Roy Haynes was on drums, Curly Russell was on bass, and Bud Powell was on piano. So they were playing “The Song Is You,” the song that I scatted with him as I went by. And as I © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -14-

walked past the bandstand, now it had been two years and four months since I had seen him for about nine minutes on this bandstand in Toledo, which is the heart of nowhere. And as I walked past the bandstand, he’s playing [scats], “hey Jon, how you doin’ man, you want to sing some?” I almost fainted. It took my breath away. I said good Lord, who the hell is that? I couldn’t believe that. And after the set he came over to my table, sat down, talked to me and just said, “what you doing?” And I said, “well I just got here.” He says, “well I told everybody about you.” And he had. I had no trouble making entree into the jazz scene. Miles knew me, Dizzy knew me, all the cats knew me. Kenny Dorham knew me because he was there in Toledo. So I had the best PR man in the world. So I came in, I just slid in. It was amazing. And that’s how I got my start in New York. He really did talk about me, and some of the cats told me, or Dizzy told me Bird told him, “man there’s a bad cat in Toledo.”

And I only saw him about three more times. Because he was running in the netherworld I called it, because it was a world of trying to get high, trying to get ahold of some horse or some money to get some horse, and to shoot up and all that, and I was not interested in that so I never really spent a lot of time with him. I would see him and his first concern would be, “how are you? How is everything? Is everything all right? Do you need anything?” He’s asking me if I need anything. And he’s looking for some dope and didn’t have any money himself, but he’s asking me if I need anything. Amazing.
